Nestled in the heart of Hanoi, specifically within the picturesque Tay Ho District, lies the serene expanse of West Lake, the largest natural freshwater lake in the city. This vast body of water, a shimmering emerald gem, stretches gracefully along the winding roads, offering a tranquil contrast to the bustling urban life nearby.

Historically, West Lake traces its origins back to the ancient Red River, remnants of which were left behind when the river altered its course over millennia. According to local lore, the lake was once known as đầm Xác Cáo, or "Fox Corpse Pond," due to a legendary tale involving a nine-tailed fox spirit subdued by the mythical figure Lạc Long Quân, whose footprints bled into the earth, forming the lake.
